issues.description: There is a direct contradiction between the Introduction and the Procedure regarding the placement of the interventions. The Introduction explicitly states the interventions are placed BEFORE collaborative recall to inoculate participants before misinformation exposure. However, the Procedure section clearly lists the interventions as Phase 3, occurring AFTER collaborative recall (Phase 2). For a registered report, this ambiguity is unacceptable as it is unclear what the actual procedure will be, and the theoretical rationale (inoculation before exposure) directly conflicts with the described procedure (intervention after exposure).
issues.quote: What is important, we decided to place the methods inducing resistance to misinformation before the collaborative recall phase (that is, before exposing participants to misinformation). The main reason for that is that we wanted to inoculate participants against the influence of misinformation before it could take effect.

issues.description: The Procedure section states the individual memory test will use 20 open-ended questions, but the Analysis Plan section states the test will use two-alternative forced-choice format. These are fundamentally different test formats that yield different types of data and have different psychometric properties. The scoring system described is based on forced-choice logic, which is incompatible with open-ended questions that could produce 'other' responses.
issues.quote: The test will contain 20 open-ended questions, eight of which will cover all the critical details [...] In the present research, the individual memory test will also use the two-alternative forced-choice format.

issues.description: The Design section claims discussed and non-discussed items are fully counterbalanced, but the Procedure section states all pairs discuss the same set of four critical details. If the same four items are always discussed, then discussed vs. non-discussed is completely confounded with item content. Any difference between discussed and non-discussed items could be due to item difficulty rather than the effect of discussion/misinformation.
issues.quote: discussed and non-discussed items will be fully counterbalanced [...] In order to ensure sufficient discussion, each pair will discuss the same set of four critical details during the collaborative recall phase. For example, all pairs will talk about Eric's cap color and his company logo.

issues.description: Both members of each pair are exposed to the same condition and interact during collaborative recall, creating statistical dependency within pairs. The planned ANOVA treats individual participants as independent observations, violating the independence assumption. This inflates the effective sample size for between-group comparisons and can produce biased standard errors. Multilevel modeling or pair-level analysis should be used.
issues.quote: Pairs of participants will be randomly assigned to one of four groups [...] The results will be analyzed by means of a two-factor ANOVA

issues.description: The power analysis for the memory conformity effect synthesizes only two effect sizes (g = 1.92 and g = 0.38) using random-effects meta-analysis. With only two studies, between-study variance (tau-squared) cannot be reliably estimated. The resulting pooled effect of 1.13 is highly uncertain. Furthermore, the five-fold difference between the two effect sizes suggests fundamental heterogeneity that a simple synthesis cannot resolve.
issues.quote: The existing results as regards effect sizes are Hedges' g = 1.92, N = 55 (Ito et al., 2019) and Hedges' g = 0.38, N = 74 (Kękuś et al., 2020). Given the rather large difference in effect sizes between both studies, random effects were assumed while calculating the joint effect size, which was 1.13.

issues.description: The power analysis treats N=240 as 240 independent units, but since pairs are randomized together and are non-independent, the effective N for between-group comparisons is 120 pairs (30 per group), not 240 individuals (60 per group). This substantially reduces statistical power beyond what is reported.
issues.quote: a sample of 240 participants was assumed; this allows for excellent power to detect medium and large effect sizes

issues.description: The Extended Warning condition includes 'enlightenment' — revealing to participants that their partner actually saw a different movie version — while the Education and Demonstration conditions apparently do not include this revelation. This means the Extended Warning condition confounds the warning content with knowledge of the deception, making it impossible to attribute any observed effects specifically to the warning versus the deception revelation.
issues.quote: an enlightenment regarding the purpose of the deception [...] Extended warning, informing that the partner actually saw a different version of the movie and informing why the deception was applied

issues.description: The three interventions differ substantially in format, duration, and interactivity. Extended Warning and Education are passive ~7-minute podcasts, while Demonstration and Motivation involves an interactive DRM task with feedback plus a podcast. Differences in outcomes could be due to the format (active vs. passive engagement, total time) rather than the theoretical content of the interventions.
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast [...] The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast [...] a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used [...] Next, the participants' motivation to resist memory suggestibility will consist in them listening to a podcast

issues.description: The control group listens to a podcast about 'soft skills related to social attitudes.' Content about social attitudes could prime social conformity concepts, potentially affecting the very social influence processes underlying memory conformity. An unrelated topic (e.g., geography, nature) would be a more neutral control.
issues.quote: In the control group, participants will listen to a podcast concerning soft skills related to social attitudes.

issues.subcategory: lack of manipulation check for misinformation exposure
issues.description: The analysis plan states that all discussed items will be categorized as containing misinformation, regardless of whether the partner actually provided discrepant information. During collaborative recall, partners might agree, fail to discuss the critical detail, or one partner might adopt the other's version. Without verifying that misinformation was actually delivered (despite audio recording being mentioned), the classification of 'misled' items is inaccurate.
issues.quote: while scoring the individual memory test accuracy on the discussed questions (items containing misleading information), we will categorize all discussed items as having contained misinformation, as the collaborative recall procedure is designed to expose participants to their partner's differing version of events.

issues.description: In the Demonstration and Motivation condition, both members of a pair appear to undergo the DRM procedure together and receive feedback about memory fallibility together. This shared experience could prompt meta-discussion about memory reliability between partners, potentially revealing the MORI deception or creating additional social dynamics not present in other conditions.
issues.quote: the experimenter will give the following information to the participants: 'Thank you for completing this memory task. Please take a look at your sheets now. See if you have written down any of the words: doctor, window, sweet, thief. If so, you were fooled.'

issues.description: The exclusion criteria do not mention checking whether participants noticed that they were watching different movie versions, which is a standard and critical check in MORI technique studies (e.g., Garry et al., 2008). If participants detect the manipulation, the entire premise of the study is compromised. The hypothesis awareness check at the end is described only as 'exploratory' and not as a basis for exclusion.
issues.quote: We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

issues.description: The exclusion criteria are extremely vague, listing only 'technical problems.' No pre-specified criteria are provided for excluding participants who: (1) detected the MORI manipulation, (2) failed to discuss critical details, (3) had visual problems with polarized glasses, (4) showed poor encoding (e.g., baseline accuracy near chance), or (5) refused to participate in collaborative recall. For a registered report, precise exclusion criteria are essential.
issues.quote: We will exclude participants in the case of any technical problems during the experimental session.

issues.description: Four dependent variables are derived from the memory test (correct answers, misinformation-consistent answers, other answers, overall number of answers) plus subjective certainty ratings and exploratory analyses. No correction for multiple comparisons or family-wise error rate is mentioned in the analysis plan.
issues.quote: Four indices will be derived from the open-ended test: the number of: (1) correct answers (consistent with the movie), (2) answers consistent with the misinformation, (3) other answers (consistent neither with the movie nor the misinformation), and (4) the overall number of answers.

issues.subcategory: missing analysis plan for secondary measures
issues.description: Subjective certainty ratings (0-100%) are collected for each answer, but no analysis plan is specified for these data. Similarly, no analysis plan is provided for the hypothesis awareness data or the audio recordings of discussions. For a registered report, all planned analyses should be pre-specified.
issues.quote: for each question, the participants will be asked to rate the subjective certainty of each answer on a scale from 0% (complete uncertainty, guessing) to 100% (absolute certainty)

issues.description: There is no mention of experimenter blinding. The experimenter appears to know which condition participants are assigned to and administers the interventions directly (especially the DRM procedure with live feedback). This creates potential for experimenter demand effects and differential treatment across conditions.
issues.quote: the experimenter will give the following information to the participants: 'Thank you for completing this memory task.'

issues.description: The authors assert that normative influence is 'completely ruled out' because participants complete the memory test individually. However, normative influence during the collaborative recall phase (where partners discuss face-to-face) could produce lasting effects on memory encoding and commitment to answers. The lingering effects of normative pressure during discussion cannot be ruled out simply because the final test is individual.
issues.quote: Given the fact that the individual memory test does not include any element of direct interpersonal pressure, we assumed that the normative impact explanation of the memory conformity effect is completely ruled out in this study

issues.description: The procedure notes that if partners cannot agree during collaborative recall, both responses are documented. However, the analysis plan provides no guidance on how to handle these cases. Are these items treated as 'discussed' (misled)? The blanket classification of all discussed items as containing misinformation fails to accommodate this scenario.
issues.quote: If the participants are unable to reach an agreement, both responses will be documented.

issues.description: The analysis plan mentions follow-up pairwise comparisons if the main interaction is significant but does not specify which comparisons are planned vs. post-hoc, whether they are one-tailed or two-tailed, or what correction (if any) will be applied. The power analysis mentions directional tests, but the analysis plan does not formalize this.
issues.quote: In the case of a significant main interaction, follow-up comparisons between pairs of groups will be performed. [...] Comparisons among all groups and directional significance tests are assumed.

issues.description: The age range is restricted to 16-35 years, and participants are self-selected through media/internet advertisements. This convenience sample limits generalizability to real-world witness populations, which span a wider age range. Additionally, including minors (16-17) may introduce developmental confounds that are not addressed.
issues.quote: The participants enrolled in the study will be 16–35 years old; they will be invited to participate via advertisements in the media and on the internet.

issues.description: The authors acknowledge substantial overlap between conditions (e.g., teaching about memory appears in both Education and Demonstration conditions), yet no attempt is made to isolate specific active ingredients or design conditions that allow disambiguation of mechanisms. This limits the ability to draw conclusions about why any particular intervention worked or failed.
issues.quote: Secondly, we are aware of some overlap between the three interventions, for instance, teaching about memory is included is present in a way in both Education about memory and Demonstration and motivation.

issues.description: A within-subjects correlation of r = 0.07 was used in the power analysis, derived from only two prior studies. This near-zero correlation is unusually low for repeated-measures designs and may be an unreliable estimate. If the true correlation is higher, the study would be overpowered for the within-subjects effect but the between-within interaction power estimates would change.
issues.quote: The joint correlation of results in the discussed and non-discussed items in both studies available was 0.07.

issues.description: The theoretical framework draws heavily on inoculation theory (McGuire, 1964) and Sagarin et al. (2002), which involve preparing people BEFORE exposure to influence. If the interventions are applied after collaborative recall (as the Procedure states), the inoculation framework is not appropriate because participants have already been exposed to the influence. The interventions would function more as post-warnings or retrieval aids rather than inoculation.
issues.quote: The main reason for that is that we wanted to inoculate participants against the influence of misinformation before it could take effect. In reality, it is most effective to prepare a witness before possible misinformation reaches them.

issues.subcategory: missing effect size specification for hypothesized ordering
issues.description: The authors hypothesize a specific ordering of intervention effectiveness (Demonstration > Extended Warning > Education > Control) but provide no planned statistical test for this directional hypothesis (e.g., trend analysis, ordered contrasts) and no basis for what effect size differences between methods are expected.
issues.quote: we tentatively assume that the most effective technique in reducing the memory conformity effect will be Demonstration and motivation [...] the Extended warning against misinformation is expected to be slightly less effective than Demonstration and motivation but more effective than Education about memory.

issues.description: The Demonstration and Motivation condition assumes most participants will falsely recall critical lures in the DRM task. However, with only four word lists and a substantially shortened procedure, the DRM effect may not be reliably produced in all participants. If some participants do not produce false memories, the 'demonstration of vulnerability' fails for those individuals. No contingency plan is provided for participants who do not show the DRM effect.
issues.quote: The DRM procedure usually results in most of the participants falsely recalling at least a few of the critical lures. Four lists will be chosen which on the basis of our previous research with this procedure, produce the strongest effect.

issues.subcategory: incomplete specification of analysis for exploratory DRM predictor
issues.description: The analysis plan mentions using DRM results as a predictor of MORI results but provides no detail on the statistical approach (regression? correlation? what outcome variable?). This is underspecified even for an exploratory analysis.
issues.quote: As an additional exploratory analysis, the results on the DRM procedure will be used as a possible predictor of the results on the MORI technique.

issues.description: The Extended Warning condition explicitly reveals the deception and explains the misinformation effect. This could create strong demand characteristics where participants simply learn what the 'correct' answer strategy is (choose own memory over partner's) rather than genuinely improving memory monitoring. The effect would be indistinguishable from genuine memory protection.
issues.quote: a clear warning that the partner might have been wrong during the collaborative recall; an extensive lecture on the nature of the misinformation effect [...] an enlightenment regarding the purpose of the deception.

issues.description: The analysis plan does not specify the significance level (alpha) that will be used for hypothesis testing. For a registered report, this should be pre-specified.
issues.quote: The hypothesis concerning the efficacy of the methods for reducing the memory conformity effect will be verified by means of analyzing the interaction between the repeated measures factor of misinformation and the grouping factor.

issues.description: The analysis plan does not address how missing data, non-responses, or 'don't know' answers on the individual memory test will be handled. Given that open-ended questions are mentioned, participants may provide ambiguous, partial, or no responses, and scoring rules for these cases are not specified.
issues.quote: The test will contain 20 open-ended questions, eight of which will cover all the critical details included in the movie

issues.description: The Demonstration and Motivation condition involves an interactive DRM task plus feedback plus a podcast, which likely takes considerably longer than the ~7-minute podcasts in the other two experimental conditions. Differential retention intervals between the collaborative recall and the individual memory test could confound results, as longer delays generally impair memory.
issues.quote: The extended warning will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast [...] The training will take the form of an approximately 7-minute podcast [...] a substantially shortened and simplified procedure based on the DRM paradigm will be used

issues.description: The analysis plan relies on ANOVA but does not discuss how assumptions (normality, sphericity, homogeneity of variance) will be assessed or what alternatives will be used if assumptions are violated. With count data from only 4 discussed and 4 non-discussed items, distributions may be non-normal and floor/ceiling effects are likely.
issues.quote: We will explore the individual memory test's scores for the critical details using analysis of variance (ANOVA)

issues.description: Only 8 critical items exist (4 discussed, 4 non-discussed), meaning each condition's score is based on very few observations per participant. This limits reliability of within-subject measures and statistical power, and makes the measures highly sensitive to individual item properties.
issues.quote: Both versions are identical except for eight critical details [...] the participants will discuss half of the discrepant details
